description: Practice management for the firm: time tracking, billing and invoicing, retainers, proposals and engagement letters, WIP reporting, a client portal, and document intake.
_doc: In-tree manifest for KisaesDevLab/Vibe-Time-Billing (github.com/KisaesDevLab/Vibe-Time-Billing). ONE GHCR mono-image runs three tiers plus a one-shot: `vibe-time-billing-api` (Express, :3001, /health, migrates itself at boot via ops/docker/entrypoint-api.sh), `vibe-time-billing-worker` (BullMQ jobs, same image, no HTTP surface), and `vibe-time-billing-web` (caddy:2-alpine serving the staff/portal/intake SPA dists that `vibe-time-billing-init` copies out of the image together with the app's own ops/docker/Caddyfile — the appliance vendors nothing; the config ships inside the image). REALMS: the app splits staff (web:80 catch-all) from the client portal (Host `portal.*` on :80, or the :8088 listener) with separate cookie names and JWT secrets; all browser traffic must flow through the web tier, so routing declares NO /api matcher — the single matcher is named `api` ONLY because the seed runner and health prober key on that name to reach the API container, and its path is the bare /health passthrough. ROOT-SERVED: the SPA dists are built with base '/' and no 40-base-path.sh hook, so the app cannot be path-mounted (rootServedOnly) — domain mode serves it at practice.<domain> + portal.<domain>; LAN/Tailscale access is the emergency ports (5178 staff, 5179 portal — 5179 maps to web:8088, which IS the portal realm listener, so the split survives without hostnames). UPDATE CAVEAT: update.sh's scoped stop/up covers web+api (routing-derived); the worker shares the api image and picks up the new one on the next enable — run Disable/Enable after an update if worker-side jobs must move immediately (same accepted limitation as vibe-1040's sidecar). NOT WIRED (owned by the appliance instead, per the no-app-owned-infra rule): the app's built-in Cloudflare-tunnel provisioning, backup sidecar mounts, and recovery-kit volume are all omitted; those admin pages will report their feature unavailable. OpenSign e-sign is upstream-standalone opt-in (OPENSIGN_URL unset = native signing). STORAGE: ships STORAGE_PROVIDER=mock so first enable succeeds for evaluation, but mock storage is THROWAWAY — real client documents require the firm's Backblaze B2 bucket (Settings → Storage) before production use.

subdomains.name: portal
subdomains.emergencyNote: Staff emergency access only — portal magic-link and payment flows require HTTPS cookies and won't work over the plain-HTTP emergency port.

required.name: STAFF_JWT_SECRET
required.doc: Signs staff sessions. Per-app and per-realm — the portal uses its own secret so rotating one realm never signs out the other.

required.name: PORTAL_JWT_SECRET
required.doc: Signs client-portal sessions. Distinct from STAFF_JWT_SECRET by upstream design (realm isolation).

required.name: KMS_KEY
required.doc: 32 raw bytes, base64. Envelope-encryption master key; the api refuses to boot without it. NOT ROTATABLE IN PLACE — losing it loses every wrapped data key. Generated once on first enable and preserved on every re-render; lives in /opt/vibe/env inside the appliance's sealed backup set.

required.name: PROPOSAL_SIGNATURE_HMAC_SEED
required.doc: Seeds the HMAC on proposal-signature links minted by the worker. Generated once and preserved.

required.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
required.doc: Password for the seeded firm admin (see firstLogin). Consumed by the run-once seed only; change the password in-app afterwards — the seed will not reset it again.

optional.name: VIBE_APP_SUBDOMAIN
optional.doc: Operator override for this app's subdomain label. Empty = the manifest default (practice). Consumed by the appliance routing (Caddy vhost + Cloudflare Tunnel CNAME/ingress); because this app is rootServedOnly it is served at its own subdomain in BOTH routing modes. Single DNS label — lowercase letters, digits, dashes, no dots.

ui.label: Subdomain
ui.helpText: The <subdomain> in <subdomain>.<your-domain> for the staff app. Leave blank for the default (practice). Lowercase letters, digits, and dashes; no dots. Saving re-renders routing and re-provisions the Cloudflare Tunnel; the app briefly restarts.

optional.name: STORAGE_PROVIDER
optional.doc: Object-storage backend for client documents: b2 (Backblaze B2 — production) or mock (in-process, THROWAWAY — evaluation only, documents do not survive). The appliance ships mock so first enable succeeds; switch to b2 with the fields below before storing real client documents.

ui.label: Document storage backend
ui.helpText: mock is evaluation-only — uploaded documents are NOT durable. For production, create a Backblaze B2 bucket (firm-owned), fill in the B2 fields below, and set this to b2. The app restarts on save.

optional.name: B2_ENDPOINT
optional.doc: Backblaze B2 S3-compatible endpoint, e.g. https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com.

ui.label: B2 endpoint
ui.helpText: From the B2 bucket's details page, e.g. https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com.

ui.label: B2 region
ui.helpText: The region segment of the endpoint, e.g. us-west-004.

optional.name: B2_BUCKET
optional.doc: B2 bucket name (private bucket the firm owns).

ui.label: B2 bucket
ui.helpText: A private bucket the firm owns. The app never shares these credentials with third parties.

optional.name: B2_KEY_ID
optional.doc: B2 application key id, scoped to the bucket.

ui.label: B2 key ID
ui.helpText: Create an application key restricted to the bucket above.

ui.label: B2 application key
ui.helpText: The secret half of the application key. Stored in the per-app env file (mode 600).

optional.name: MAIL_SMTP_HOST
optional.doc: SMTP relay host. Sign-in REQUIRES working email (magic links and emailed one-time codes), so configure this before the first login.

ui.label: SMTP host
ui.helpText: Sign-in emails (magic links, one-time codes), invoices, and client notifications all go through this relay. Required before first login.

ui.label: SMTP port
ui.helpText: 587 for STARTTLS (typical), 465 for implicit TLS, 25 for plain relays.

ui.label: SMTP username
ui.helpText: Leave blank for an unauthenticated relay.

ui.label: SMTP password
ui.helpText: Stored in the per-app env file (mode 600).

optional.name: MAIL_FROM
optional.doc: From header for outbound mail, e.g. "Smith & Co CPAs <billing@smithcpas.com>".

ui.label: Mail from address
ui.helpText: Shown on sign-in, invoice, and portal emails. Use an address your SMTP relay is allowed to send as.

firstLogin.note: The username is whatever ADMIN_EMAIL was at enable time (default admin@appliance.local — set a real address in /opt/vibe/env/vibe-time-billing.env BEFORE first enable). IMPORTANT: sign-in requires working EMAIL — password login is completed with an emailed one-time code, and magic-link login is email too — so configure the SMTP settings (Settings → this app → Email & SMS) before the first login or you cannot get in. Change the password in-app after signing in; the seed runs once and will not reset it. This app is served at the ROOT of its own subdomain in both routing modes (rootServedOnly), so in LAN/Tailscale mode use http://<server-ip>:5178/ for the staff app and http://<server-ip>:5179/ for the client portal.

seed.description: Two upstream run-once scripts, chained: bootstrap-firm creates the minimal firm (one office, service lines, rate code, notification templates) from FIRM_NAME/ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_NAME; create-admin then attaches the admin role and sets the ADMIN_PASSWORD password with email-OTP second factor. Both are idempotent upstream, and state.apps.vibe-time-billing.seeded gates the pair to a single run. All inputs come from the per-app env file — set FIRM_NAME and ADMIN_EMAIL there BEFORE first enable.
